freeScan.opening:
Howdy Ben!

Thanks for letting me look at your winter. You've got an 8-year-old and a 12-year-old, a season around Sugarbush, Bolton Valley, and Smugglers' Notch, plus a couple trips that aren't local.

Here's what I'd pay attention to.
freeScan.savingsLine: I found roughly $1,100-$1,900 that looks worth a look.

findings.heading: The France week is the one I'd settle first
findings.explanation: If that trip is still on, there is a much cheaper way to buy the week than treating it like a Colorado window ticket. I'll keep the exact details in the full Plan.

findings.heading: Breckenridge only if you actually go
findings.explanation: Your current Vermont setup does not cover that mountain. If the trip happens, buy the right product in advance. If it doesn't, skip it.

findings.heading: Something worth a look at Bolton Valley
findings.explanation: At your day count, a couple of the close mountains stop making sense as one-off tickets.

cta.headline: Want the full details?
cta.body:
I already put together the complete Savings Plan with the exact programs, who qualifies, deadlines, and links. If you'd like it, it's $49.

If you get it and don't feel it was worth $49, tell me. I'll refund you. You can keep the Plan.

opportunities.title: France family skipass pricing
opportunities.found: If the Alps week is still on, buy the official family or youth product for those dates. US-style window math is the expensive way to do that trip.
opportunities.saveNote: $850-$1,100 if you buy the official family product instead of four adult-priced tickets.
opportunities.action: Pick the resort, then buy the official family or youth skipass for your dates before lodging gets so locked that you stop caring about lift math.
opportunities.catchNote: Kids need to be in that resort's published youth ages. Your 8- and 12-year-old are usually fine. Confirm the exact band.
opportunities.deadline: Buy once dates are firm. These packs are usually date-specific.

opportunities.title: Breckenridge advance tickets
opportunities.found: Your Vermont pass setup does not cover Summit County. If this trip happens, buy the matching advance product. If it gets dropped, this save disappears with it.
opportunities.saveNote: $400-$650 only if the Breckenridge trip actually happens.
opportunities.action: Count the days. Buy the matching advance product before you go, or drop the trip from the savings story.
opportunities.catchNote: Read the calendar on the exact product before you buy. This does not stack with your Vermont pass.

opportunities.title: Bolton Valley season product
opportunities.found: Bolton is close and easy to overpay for one day at a time. At 16-30 days, some of those days are going to land here.
opportunities.saveNote: $180-$250 if the people who actually ski Bolton are on a season or multi-day product.
opportunities.action: Decide who actually skis Bolton. Put those people on a Bolton product while preseason pricing still exists.
opportunities.catchNote: Only counts if you will actually ski Bolton more than a couple of times. Do not buy four of everything.
opportunities.deadline: Preseason pass pricing is the whole point.

steps.title: Price the France week on the official family product
steps.description: This is the biggest number on the page. Pick the resort, then buy the official family or youth pack for your dates.

steps.title: Decide if Breckenridge is actually happening
steps.description: If you are going, buy the advance product. If you are not, this $400-$650 disappears, and that's fine.

steps.title: Stop buying Bolton one day at a time
steps.description: Decide who actually skis it and put them on a Bolton product while preseason pricing still exists.

knownSavings.title: Sugarbush access you already have
knownSavings.note: You already told me this is in the mix, so I left it out of the found number.

watch.title: Vermont 5th Grade Ski Passport
watch.whatWeAreWatching: Your 8-year-old is in 3rd grade. This is not a save this season. It is a save the year they hit 5th.

watchIntro: Not counted yet. Worth a calendar reminder, not a purchase today.
